questions.q: Which sentence should come FIRST after the rearrangement?
questions.solution: B introduces the older view of parks as an optional amenity. Other sentences refer back to this perception or its changed interpretation.
questions.passage:
English Language
Rearrange the following six sentences (A), (B), (C), (D), (E) and (F) in a logical sequence to form a coherent and
meaningful paragraph, and then answer the questions given below.
(A) Despite this growing evidence, access to quality green space remains starkly unequal within most cities, with
wealthier neighbourhoods typically enjoying far more parkland per resident than lower-income districts.
(B) For much of the twentieth century, urban parks were often regarded as a pleasant amenity rather than a civic
necessity, something a city might add once more pressing infrastructure needs had been met.
(C) Compounding this imbalance, the dense, built-up character of many city centres leaves little vacant land
available for new parks, and what land does remain is often prohibitively expensive to acquire.
(D) This perception has shifted considerably in recent years, as researchers have documented the tangible role
that trees and green cover play in lowering local temperatures during increasingly frequent heatwaves, a
phenomenon known as the urban heat island effect.
(E) Faced with this constraint, a number of cities have instead begun converting disused infrastructure, such as
old elevated rail lines and underused rooftops, into accessible green corridors.
(F) Beyond this cooling effect, epidemiological studies have also linked regular access to green space with
measurable improvements in residents' mental health and levels of physical activity.

questions.q: Which sentence should come SECOND after the rearrangement?
questions.solution: D follows B because this perception refers to the older attitude to parks, then introduces cooling evidence.

questions.q: The (A) outdated dial-up modem, still used in a handful of remote villages, needed (B) nearly three minutes to load a single low-resolution webpage, while the (C) modern fiber-optic connection, installed in most metropolitan offices, needed (D) under thirty seconds to download an entire high-definition film.
questions.solution: The old modem’s slow loading and the modern connection’s quick download are consistent. No interchange is needed.

questions.q: The newly hired employee took a keen _____ in the bank's new digital-lending platform during her first week, and later learned that customers who repaid their loans early were charged no additional _____ on the outstanding amount.
questions.solution: Interest means curiosity in the first blank and a borrowing charge in the second.

questions.q: Before submitting the final report, the manager asked her assistant to prepare a rough _____ for review, and later that afternoon the same assistant visited the bank to collect a _____ payable to the vendor.
questions.solution: Draft means a preliminary written version and also a bank payment instrument.

questions.q: After months of practice, the gymnast could finally maintain perfect _____ on the beam without wobbling, while her brother, a bank teller, spent the morning helping customers check their account _____ at the counter.
questions.solution: Balance means physical steadiness on the beam and the amount held in an account.

questions.q: The head chef of the newly renovated restaurant (A) / have spent the entire morning personally selecting the freshest ingredients (B) / from the local market (C) / before the critic's much-anticipated visit that evening. (D) / No error (E)
questions.solution: The singular subject head chef requires has spent, not have spent. The error is in B.

questions.q: Ever since she signed up for her first marathon six months ago, (A) / the young runner trains every single day before dawn, (B) / gradually increasing her distance each week (C) / to prepare her body for the gruelling 42-kilometre race. (D) / No error (E)
questions.solution: Ever since introduces an action continuing from the past. Use has trained or has been training instead of trains in B.

questions.q: The head librarian spent the afternoon carefully cleaning the fragile pages, (A) / repairing the torn bindings, (B) / and to catalogue each manuscript's provenance (C) / before returning them to the climate- controlled archive. (D) / No error (E)
questions.solution: The list needs parallel forms: cleaning,repairing,cataloguing. Replace to catalogue in C with cataloguing.

questions.q: Despite having flown this route hundreds of times before, the veteran pilot (A) / calmly reassured the anxious passengers (B) / that she was fully capable to handle (C) / even the most severe turbulence they might encounter. (D) / No error (E)
questions.solution: The construction is capable of handling, not capable to handle. Part C contains the error.

questions.q: After examining the injured golden eagle's wing carefully, (A) / the veterinarian concluded that the fracture, though serious, (B) / would heal completely within eight weeks (C) / provided that the bird remained in a controlled, stress-free environment. (D) / No error (E)
questions.solution: The participial opening correctly refers to the veterinarian, and the rest has consistent tense and grammar. No error.

questions.q: Choose the most appropriate word for blank (1).
questions.solution: A poor monsoon can lower output, so reduce crop yields is the appropriate expression.
questions.passage:
In the following passage, there are five blanks, each followed by a number corresponding to a question with five
options. Choose the option that fits each blank most appropriately.
Ensuring reliable access to sufficient, nutritious food for a growing global population has become one of the most
pressing challenges of this century. Climate change has made rainfall patterns increasingly erratic, and a single
poor monsoon can now (1)_____ crop yields across entire regions, pushing food prices sharply upward.

Governments have traditionally responded by maintaining large buffer stocks of staple grains, which can be
(2)_____ into the market during shortages to stabilise prices. Yet critics note that such stockpiling schemes are

expensive to maintain and prone to storage losses from pests and spoilage. In recent years, policymakers have
therefore begun to (3)_____ investment toward improving cold-chain logistics and crop-resistant seed varieties,ai
ming to prevent post-harvest losses rather than merely stockpile surplus grain after the fact. Some economists
argue that without parallel efforts to (4)_____ farmers' incomes, these technical fixes will do little to address the
deeper economic vulnerability that leaves smallholders exposed to a single bad season. Unless food policy
becomes more (5)_____, treating production, storage, and farmer welfare as a single interconnected system,
gains made in one area will continue to be undermined by neglect in another.

questions.q: Choose the most appropriate word for blank (2).
questions.solution: Buffer grain is released into the market during shortages to increase supply.
